result: RIM-BP2 knockout mice show reduced Ca2+ currents (~30%) at hippocampal mossy fiber terminals. This reduction in Ca2+ influx was measured by direct presynaptic patch-clamp recordings and represents a decrease in the number of Ca2+ channels rather than changes in activation kinetics.
evaluation: All three reviewers acknowledge this finding. The editor states the article 'provides compelling evidence demonstrating reduced calcium channel abundance in mossy terminals upon RIM-BP2 removal.' Reviewer 1 notes 'the authors demonstrate reduced Ca2+ currents' as part of 'a large body of high quality work.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'they provide solid data showing that RIM-BP2 KO reduces Ca influx at MF-CA3 synapse.'

result: STED microscopy revealed reduced abundance of P/Q-type Ca2+ channels (Cav2.1) at active zones in RIM-BP2 KO mice. The total signal intensity of Cav2.1 was 22% lower in KO mice, with no change in cluster number, suggesting reduced channel abundance per cluster.
evaluation: The reviewers accept this finding as supporting the electrophysiological data. The editor notes the study 'provides compelling evidence demonstrating reduced calcium channel abundance.' Reviewer 1 acknowledges the 'careful analysis' and Reviewer 2 confirms the STED microscopy showed 'slight decrease in cluster intensity (~20%),' which aligns with the reported 22% reduction.

result: Effects of RIM-BP2 deletion on the readily releasable pool (RRP) size and time course of release measured by capacitance measurements are relatively minor. The total signal intensity of Munc13-1 did not significantly differ between WT and RIM-BP2 KO.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings but note their implications. Reviewer 2 states 'no impacts on Ca-induced exocytosis and RRP (measured by capacitance change).' Reviewer 1 notes 'the effects are relatively small' but considers the work 'high quality.' The minor effects on RRP are consistently reported across the manuscript.

result: The initial release probability was lowered in RIM-BP2 KO due to both reduced Ca2+ influx and impaired fusion competence. The reduction in EPSC amplitudes could not be fully explained by reduced Ca2+ influx alone, suggesting an additional mechanism independent of Ca2+ influx.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly questions this interpretation, stating the authors 'propose an altered fusion competence of the SVs, which is not so strongly supported by the data in my view.' While the reduced release probability is accepted, the claim of impaired fusion competence as a separate mechanism is not strongly supported according to at least one reviewer.

result: Larger Ca2+ influx (by increasing external Ca2+ concentration to 4 mM) restored release partially in RIM-BP2 KO, making the time course of exocytosis and capacitance changes similar to WT at 2 mM Ca2+.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding. Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'can restore release by increasing Ca2+ influx.' This result is presented as part of the evidence that reduced Ca2+ influx is a primary mechanism, and reviewers do not challenge this interpretation.

result: WT and RIM-BP2 KO terminals had similar sensitivity of neurotransmitter release to EGTA, and the nearest-neighboring distance between Cav2.1 and Munc13-1 clusters was unchanged. This suggests that changes in coupling distance are not responsible for the reduced exocytosis.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding without challenge. Reviewer 2 notes the study concluded 'RIM-BP2 function in tonic synapses by reducing CaV expression and thus differentially from phasic synapses by decoupling CaV-SV,' implicitly accepting that decoupling was not observed at mossy fiber synapses.

result: RIM-BP2 regulates both Ca2+ channel abundance and transmitter release at mossy fiber synapses. At hippocampal mossy fiber terminals with low release probability, RIM-BP2 KO decreased the abundance of P/Q-type Ca2+ channels, thereby reducing Ca2+ influx and neurotransmitter release.
evaluation: This is the main conclusion and is accepted by all reviewers. The editor states the article 'addresses an important question' and provides 'compelling evidence.' Reviewer 1 calls it 'an important contribution' and Reviewer 2 acknowledges the 'solid data' though notes the phenotype is 'not new' compared to other systems.

result: The observation of reduced Ca2+ channel abundance in RIM-BP2 KO mossy fiber terminals is similar to findings at Drosophila NMJ and hair cell synapses, but differs from other mammalian synapses, suggesting that the functional role of RIM-BP2 in recruiting Ca2+ channels differs among synapse types.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly acknowledges this point, noting 'the phenotype is not new as Moser and colleagues have also used presynaptic recording and capacitance measurement and shown that RIM-BP2 KO reduces Ca2+ influx at hair cell active zone (Krinner et al., 2017)' and that 'the concept that RIM-BP2 plays diverse functions in transmitter release at different central synapses has also been proposed with solid evidence (Brockmann et al., 2019).'
